question: What is the difference between a Job and a CronJob in Kubernetes, and what does each define in its spec?

ground_truth.answer: A Job creates one or more Pods and tracks their completion. JobSpec defines parallelism (maximum simultaneous Pods), completions (required successful Pod completions), and backoffLimit (maximum retries before the Job is marked failed). The Job terminates once the required completions are reached. A CronJob creates a new Job on a recurring schedule. CronJobSpec defines a schedule field in standard cron format and a jobTemplate (a JobTemplateSpec) describing the Job to create on each invocation. Jobs suit one-off or parallelized batch work; CronJobs suit periodic recurring tasks.
context: io.k8s.api.batch.v1.Job: creates one or more Pods and tracks successful completions; terminates when the completions count is reached
io.k8s.api.batch.v1.JobSpec: defines parallelism, completions, and backoffLimit for a Job
io.k8s.api.batch.v1.CronJob: creates a new Job on a recurring schedule defined by a cron expression
io.k8s.api.batch.v1.CronJobSpec: defines schedule in cron format and jobTemplate (JobTemplateSpec) for each invocation
